note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Instruction-tuning shifts misinformation susceptibility toward the user role

nodes.name: Instruction-tuning raises input reliance
nodes.description: Instruction-tuning may heighten LLMs' dependence on user inputs, making them follow external information even when it conflicts with their parametric knowledge, which can produce hallucinations from user-provided misinformation.

nodes.name: Prior work lacks causal analysis
nodes.description: Prior studies on knowledge conflicts mostly identified that LLMs accept contradicting evidence, without investigating the direct impact of instruction-tuning as a cause.

nodes.name: MSR metric definition
nodes.description: Misinformation Susceptibility Rate is the percentage of questions answered correctly closed-book (parametric knowledge) for which the LLM, given misinformation, selects the incorrect option aligned with the misinformation.

nodes.name: Three presentation scenarios
nodes.description: Misinformation is presented as part of a single user turn (STQ), in a separate assistant-role turn (APD), or in a separate user-role turn (UPD), with the same system prompt and final user question 'What is the correct answer?'.

nodes.name: Farm dataset setup
nodes.description: Experiments use Farm questions from BoolQ, NQ and TruthfulQA that GPT-4 answers closed-book, with misinformation supporting an incorrect option, on GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Llama-3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 (instruct and base).

nodes.name: User role more susceptible than assistant
nodes.description: Except for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, all instruction-tuned models have higher MSR in UPD than APD across all datasets, so misinformation is accepted more when presented through the user role.

nodes.name: Separate user turn amplifies susceptibility
nodes.description: Across all models and datasets, UPD has higher MSR than STQ (typically 5-8 percentage points, averaging 22 points for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3), so separating misinformation into its own user turn increases susceptibility.

nodes.name: Assistant role handled inconsistently
nodes.description: STQ vs APD gives mixed results across models: some (Llama-3-8B-Instruct) have lower MSR in APD than STQ, showing they disregard the assistant role, while others (Mistral, Qwen2.5) show slightly higher MSR in APD.

nodes.name: Base models favor assistant role
nodes.description: All four base models rank APD highest in MSR consistently across the three datasets, and three of four (not Qwen2.5-7B) rank UPD above STQ, so base models weight the assistant role most.

nodes.name: Instruction-tuning shifts to user role
nodes.description: After instruction-tuning, three of four open-source models (not Qwen2.5-7B) drop APD in MSR ranking and show UPD as the highest, so instruction-tuning reduces reliance on the assistant role and increases the user role's influence.

nodes.name: Instruction-tuning is the direct cause
nodes.description: The high user-role susceptibility of instruction-tuned LLMs is not merely a pre-training byproduct but a direct result of instruction-tuning, since it aligns the model more closely with user instructions.

nodes.name: Longer misinformation narrows the gap
nodes.description: As misinformation length increases (adding second and third paragraphs), the UPD-APD MSR gap mostly narrows and sometimes reverses (e.g. Llama-3-8B-Instruct), so models revert toward the base-model pattern.

nodes.name: Warning helps proprietary models only
nodes.description: Adding a misinformation warning to the system prompt on NQ reduces average MSR by 69.1 points for GPT-4o and 20.1 for GPT-4o mini, but leaves open-source models nearly unchanged, and does not change the relative ranking across scenarios (except Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct).

isolated_nodes.name: Limitation: no base proprietary models
isolated_nodes.description: Base versions of GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini are unavailable, so the direct instruction-tuning comparison covers only open-source 7B-8B models.

isolated_nodes.name: Instruction-tuning prone to sycophancy
isolated_nodes.description: Human-aligned LLMs are reported to be prone to sycophancy, excessively conforming to user opinions (cited prior work).

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the susceptibility hypothesis through metric and scenario design, to the role-based findings, base-vs-instruct causal attribution, and secondary factors (length, warnings).
